Heat stroke.presentation: After several hours of strenuous activity, the patient became confused and repeatedly tried to remove clothing. Triage temperature is 41.2°C orally, heart rate 梳138/min, blood pressure 92/54 mmHg, respiratory rate 28/min, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air. Skin is hot and flushed with minimal sweating. The patient is disoriented, intermittently combative, and unable to follow commands. Point-of-care glucose is 118 mg/dL. Laboratory testing shows creatinine 2.1 mg/dL, sodium 149 mmol/L, bicarbonate 19 mmol/L, lactate 5.8 mmol/L, and creatine kinase 1,240 U/L. Chest examination is clear.
Heat stroke.context_keep: The patient had been installing exterior cladding for {employer} during the hottest part of {month}.
Heat stroke.context_generalized: The patient had been doing strenuous outdoor manual work for an employer during the hottest part of {season}.

Heat stroke.presentation: The patient arrives with severe throbbing headache, nausea, and photophobia after collapsing briefly. Temperature is 40.6°C, pulse 132/min, blood pressure 104/62 mmHg, respiratory rate 24/min, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air. The patient is drowsy but arousable, answers inconsistently, and has no focal weakness or neck rigidity. Pupils are equal and reactive. Skin is hot and damp. Glucose is 96 mg/dL; sodium is 151 mmol/L, creatinine 1.8 mg/dL, lactate 4.2 mmol/L, and creatine kinase 860 U/L. Noncontrast head CT shows no hemorrhage or mass.
Heat stroke.context_keep: Symptoms began while the patient was carrying paving materials for {employer} in {month}.
Heat stroke.context_generalized: Symptoms began during strenuous outdoor manual work in {season}.

Heat stroke.presentation: The patient is brought in after becoming unable to stand and speaking incoherently. Temperature is 42.0°C, heart rate 146/min, blood pressure 86/48 mmHg, respiratory rate 31/min, and oxygen saturation 97% on room air. The patient has generalized rigidity, marked agitation, and intermittent generalized muscle twitching. Skin is hot, dry, and mottled. Glucose is 134 mg/dL. Initial studies show potassium 5.8 mmol/L, bicarbonate 16 mmol/L, creatinine 2.7 mg/dL, lactate 7.1 mmol/L, and creatine kinase 3,900 U/L. Urinalysis is positive for blood with few red cells. ECG shows sinus tachycardia without ischemic changes.
Heat stroke.context_keep: The patient had been unloading cement bags for {employer} outdoors in {month}.
Heat stroke.context_generalized: The patient had been performing heavy outdoor manual labor in {season}.

Heat stroke.presentation: The patient presents with fever, vomiting, and altered behavior that began during the afternoon. Temperature is 40.3°C, pulse 128/min, blood pressure 101/58 mmHg, respiratory rate 26/min, and oxygen saturation 96% on room air. The patient is inattentive and intermittently confused but has no neck stiffness, photophobia, or focal neurological deficit. The abdomen is soft without guarding. Mucous membranes are dry, and sweating is scant. Sodium is 153 mmol/L, potassium 4.7 mmol/L, creatinine 2.0 mg/dL, lactate 4.9 mmol/L, and creatine kinase 1,670 U/L. Heat stroke.context_keep: The patient had been repairing roofing for {employer} without shade during {month}.
Heat stroke.context_generalized: The patient had been doing prolonged outdoor manual work without shade during {season}.

Heat stroke.presentation: The patient collapses after several hours of physical exertion and arrives with a temperature of 41.5°C, heart rate 151/min, blood pressure 88/50 mmHg, respiratory rate 30/min, and oxygen saturation 95% on room air. The patient is obtunded, withdraws from pain, and has brisk symmetric reflexes without lateralizing signs. Skin is flushed and hot; sweat is present on the trunk. Point-of-care glucose is 109 mg/dL. Venous lactate is 6.4 mmol/L, sodium 148 mmol/L, creatinine 2.4 mg/dL, AST 186 U/L, ALT 102 U/L, and creatine kinase 2,250 U/L. Bedside ultrasound shows a small, collapsible inferior vena cava.

Heat stroke.context_generalized: The collapse occurred during strenuous outdoor work involving heat-producing materials in {season}.

Heat stroke.presentation: The patient reports cramping abdominal pain, repeated watery stools, and weakness followed by confusion. Temperature is 39.8°C, pulse 126/min, blood pressure 94/56 mmHg, respiratory rate 22/min, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air. The patient is flushed, inattentive, and unable to state the location. There is no abdominal guarding or focal tenderness. Oral mucosa is dry, and sweating is minimal. Sodium is 155 mmol/L, potassium 3.2 mmol/L, bicarbonate 18 mmol/L, creatinine 2.2 mg/dL, lactate 4.6 mmol/L, and creatine kinase 710 U/L. Pre-eclampsia.presentation: A pregnant patient at 34 weeks presents with a severe frontal headache, flashing lights, and increasing swelling of the hands and face. Blood pressure is 172/112 mmHg on two readings 15 minutes apart, pulse 92/min, temperature 36.8°C, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air. There is brisk reflex activity without clonus and mild right upper-quadrant tenderness. Urine dipstick shows 3+ protein. Platelets are 108 ×10⁹/L, AST 86 U/L, ALT 74 U/L, creatinine 101 µmol/L, and LDH is elevated. Fetal heart rate is 146/min with reduced variability but no persistent decelerations.

A pregnant patient at 29 weeks arrives with abrupt severe epigastric pain, nausea, and repeated vomiting. Blood pressure is 166/104 mmHg, pulse 104/min, temperature 37.1°C, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air. The abdomen is tender in the epigastrium without guarding. Urine contains 2+ protein. Platelets are 92 ×10⁹/L, AST 142 U/L, ALT 119 U/L, bilirubin 22 µmol/L, and creatinine 118 µmol/L. Lipase is normal, hemoglobin is 10.8 g/dL, and leukocytes are 12.4 ×10⁹/L. Ultrasound shows a singleton fetus with appropriate growth and no gallstones; fetal heart rate is 150/min.
Pre-eclampsia.context_keep: She works as a {occupation} at {employer}, where she has frequent exposure to patients with vomiting and diarrhoea.
Pre-eclampsia.context_generalized: The patient works in {occupation_category}, with frequent exposure to people with vomiting and diarrhoea.

Pre-eclampsia.presentation: A pregnant patient at 37 weeks reports a persistent occipital headache and new blurred vision despite taking paracetamol. Blood pressure is 184/116 mmHg, pulse 88/min, temperature 36.7°C, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air. There is 2+ pedal oedema, brisk patellar reflexes, and one beat of ankle clonus. Urine protein-to-creatinine ratio is 92 mg/mmol. Platelets are 136 ×10⁹/L, AST 48 U/L, ALT 44 U/L, and creatinine 89 µmol/L. Fetal monitoring shows a baseline of 140/min with moderate variability and no decelerations. Chest examination is clear and there is no focal neurological deficit.

A pregnant patient at 31 weeks presents with breathlessness, chest tightness, and a dry cough that began overnight. Blood pressure is 158/102 mmHg, pulse 108/min, respiratory rate 24/min, temperature 36.9°C, and oxygen saturation 94% on room air. There are fine bibasal crackles and mild ankle oedema without wheeze. Chest radiography shows pulmonary vascular congestion without focal infiltrate. Urine protein-to-creatinine ratio is 76 mg/mmol. Platelets are 121 ×10⁹/L, AST 62 U/L, and creatinine 96 µmol/L. ECG shows sinus tachycardia; troponin is normal. Fetal heart rate is 148/min.
Pre-eclampsia.context_keep: She works as a {occupation} at {employer} and had been outdoors in the intense {month} heat immediately before the breathlessness began.
Pre-eclampsia.context_generalized: The patient works in {occupation_category} and had been outdoors in intense {season} heat immediately before the breathlessness began.

Pre-eclampsia.presentation: A pregnant patient at 35 weeks is brought in after two generalized tonic-clonic seizures. On arrival, blood pressure is 178/110 mmHg, pulse 110/min, temperature 36.6°C, and oxygen saturation 96% on room air. Postictally, there is no neck stiffness or focal weakness, but reflexes are markedly brisk. Urine dipstick shows 3+ protein. Platelets are 74 ×10⁹/L, AST 168 U/L, ALT 151 U/L, creatinine 127 µmol/L, and glucose 5.8 mmol/L. CT head shows no hemorrhage or mass. Fetal monitoring reveals recurrent late decelerations with a baseline of 160/min. There is no history of epilepsy or recent head trauma.

A pregnant patient at 28 weeks presents with feverishness, confusion, severe headache, and right-sided upper-abdominal pain. Blood pressure is 170/108 mmHg, pulse 118/min, temperature 37.8°C, respiratory rate 20/min, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air. There is no meningism or photophobia. Urine protein-to-creatinine ratio is 110 mg/mmol. Platelets are 86 ×10⁹/L, AST 201 U/L, ALT 177 U/L, creatinine 132 µmol/L, and lactate is 2.1 mmol/L. Blood cultures are negative at preliminary review; leukocytes are 14.2 ×10⁹/L. Ultrasound shows no biliary obstruction. Fetal heart rate is 155/min with reduced variability.
Pre-eclampsia.context_keep: She is visiting from {country} during {month} and had received several doses of antibiotics elsewhere for presumed infection without improvement.
Pre-eclampsia.context_generalized: The patient is visiting from {region} during {season} and had received several doses of antibiotics elsewhere for presumed infection without improvement.

Pre-eclampsia.presentation: A pregnant patient at 26 weeks presents with sudden severe shortness of breath, orthopnoea, and a nonproductive cough. Blood pressure is 174/106 mmHg, pulse 116/min, respiratory rate 30/min, temperature 36.5°C, and oxygen saturation 88% on room air. Bibasal crackles extend halfway up both lung fields, with no unilateral leg swelling. Chest radiography shows bilateral perihilar air-space shadowing and small pleural effusions. Urine protein-to-creatinine ratio is 84 mg/mmol. Platelets are 115 ×10⁹/L, AST 71 U/L, and creatinine 104 µmol/L. ECG shows sinus tachycardia without ischemic changes; troponin is normal. Fetal heart rate is 152/min.

Pre-eclampsia.context_generalized: The patient works in {occupation_category}, spending prolonged shifts around cooking fumes and initially attributing the dyspnoea to inhalation exposure.

Pre-eclampsia.presentation: A pregnant patient at 33 weeks reports malaise, nausea, dark urine, and dull right-upper-quadrant discomfort. Blood pressure is 160/100 mmHg, pulse 98/min, temperature 37.0°C, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air. There is mild scleral icterus and brisk reflexes without clonus. Urine dipstick shows 2+ protein. Platelets are 101 ×10⁹/L, AST 312 U/L, ALT 276 U/L, bilirubin 38 µmol/L, creatinine 109 µmol/L, and LDH is substantially elevated. Glucose is 4.9 mmol/L and lipase is normal. Ultrasound shows no gallstones or biliary dilatation. Fetal monitoring is reactive with a baseline of 145/min.

A pregnant patient at 30 weeks presents with severe headache, photophobia, and vomiting, describing the pain as unlike previous headaches. Blood pressure is 182/114 mmHg, pulse 94/min, temperature 36.9°C, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air. Neurological examination shows hyperreflexia and sustained ankle clonus but no papilloedema or focal deficit. Urine protein-to-creatinine ratio is 98 mg/mmol. Platelets are 97 ×10⁹/L, AST 104 U/L, ALT 91 U/L, and creatinine 115 µmol/L. CT venography shows no cerebral venous thrombosis. Fetal heart rate is 150/min with intermittent variable decelerations. There is no neck stiffness or rash.

Pre-eclampsia.context_generalized: The patient arrived after a long flight from {region} in {season}, and the headache was initially attributed to travel-related dehydration and travel fatigue.

Pre-eclampsia.presentation: A pregnant patient at 38 weeks is evaluated for new painless swelling and a feeling of pressure in the face and hands. Blood pressure is 150/96 mmHg, pulse 84/min, temperature 36.7°C, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air. There is 1+ peripheral oedema but no headache, visual symptoms, abdominal pain, or neurological deficit. Urine dipstick shows 2+ protein, with a protein-to-creatinine ratio of 42 mg/mmol. Platelets are 164 ×10⁹/L, AST 31 U/L, ALT 28 U/L, and creatinine 78 µmol/L. Fetal ultrasound shows normal growth, normal amniotic fluid, and normal umbilical artery Doppler flow. Non-stress testing is reactive.

A pregnant patient at 24 weeks presents with chest discomfort, nausea, and profound fatigue rather than headache or abdominal pain. Blood pressure is 162/105 mmHg, pulse 102/min, temperature 36.8°C, and oxygen saturation 97% on room air. The pain is nonradiating and reproducible only minimally with palpation. ECG shows sinus rhythm without ST-segment changes, and serial high-sensitivity troponin is normal. Urine protein-to-creatinine ratio is 68 mg/mmol. Platelets are 128 ×10⁹/L, AST 58 U/L, ALT 49 U/L, and creatinine 94 µmol/L. Echocardiography shows normal systolic function. Fetal heart rate is 147/min with no decelerations.

Pre-eclampsia.context_generalized: The patient works in {occupation_category} and had been working overnight in the {season} heat before the chest discomfort started.

Blood pressure is 168/106 mmHg, pulse 108/min, temperature 38.1°C, respiratory rate 23/min, and oxygen saturation 95% on room air. Chest examination reveals fine basal crackles but no focal bronchial breathing. Chest radiography shows mild bilateral interstitial oedema without consolidation. Urine protein-to-creatinine ratio is 88 mg/mmol. Platelets are 109 ×10⁹/L, AST 79 U/L, ALT 68 U/L, and creatinine 102 µmol/L. Lactate is 1.4 mmol/L; blood cultures are negative to preliminary review. Fetal monitoring shows a baseline of 150/min with moderate variability.
Pre-eclampsia.context_keep: She works as a {occupation} at {employer}, and several colleagues recently had a documented respiratory infection.
Pre-eclampsia.context_generalized: The patient works in {occupation_category}, and several colleagues recently had a documented respiratory infection.

Ectopic pregnancy.presentation: Several hours of worsening unilateral lower abdominal pain are accompanied by light vaginal bleeding and dizziness. The patient reports a missed period and a positive home pregnancy test obtained recently. On arrival, temperature is 36.8 °C, heart rate 108/min, blood pressure 102/68 mmHg, respiratory rate 18/min, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air. There is left lower-quadrant tenderness with guarding but no diffuse rigidity. Hemoglobin is 10.8 g/dL, white-cell count 9.6 × 10⁹/L, and serum β-hCG is 2,940 IU/L. Transvaginal ultrasonography shows no intrauterine gestational sac and a small amount of pelvic free fluid.

Ectopic pregnancy.context_generalized: She is a {occupation_category} and had prolonged outdoor heat exposure before the symptoms began.

Abdominal examination shows marked right iliac fossa tenderness and mild rebound. Hemoglobin is 9.7 g/dL, white-cell count 11.2 × 10⁹/L, and β-hCG is 5,180 IU/L. Ectopic pregnancy.context_generalized: She recently arrived from {region} for a family visit and has not had access to her usual reproductive healthcare.

Ectopic pregnancy.presentation: Lower abdominal discomfort, urinary frequency, and burning have been present for three days, followed by faint vaginal spotting. Ectopic pregnancy.context_generalized: She recently returned from {region}, where she was treated empirically for urinary symptoms without pregnancy testing.

Ectopic pregnancy.context_generalized: She is staying in temporary accommodation during a family visit from {region}, where several relatives recently developed gastrointestinal symptoms.

The abdomen is tender in the right lower quadrant with guarding. Hemoglobin is 9.4 g/dL, lactate is 2.6 mmol/L, and β-hCG is 6,900 IU/L. White-cell count is 14.8 × 10⁹/L, hemoglobin 10.6 g/dL, C-reactive protein 62 mg/L, and β-hCG 2,210 IU/L. Ectopic pregnancy.presentation: Recurrent brief episodes of light-headedness and lower abdominal aching have occurred for one week, with increasing fatigue and scant spotting. Pain became constant over the preceding six hours, with nausea and a brief fainting episode. Temperature is 36.7 °C, pulse 120/min, blood pressure 91/58 mmHg, respiratory rate 21/min, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air. There is significant right lower-quadrant tenderness with rebound. Suprapubic discomfort is increasing, but there is no flank pain, fever, vomiting, or visible blood. Temperature is 36.8°C, blood pressure 148/82 mmHg, heart rate 86/min, and respiratory rate 16/min. The bladder is palpable and tender above the pubic bone. Creatinine is 118 µmol/L, estimated glomerular filtration rate is 63 mL/min/1.73 m², and leukocyte count is 8.9 ×10⁹/L. Urinalysis shows no nitrites, leukocytes, or blood. A catheter drains 950 mL of clear urine.

Difficulty initiating urination, a thin intermittent stream, urgency, and nocturia have gradually worsened over a year. The patient now reports frequent small voids and a sensation of incomplete emptying, without acute pain. Temperature is 36.6°C, blood pressure 139/78 mmHg, heart rate 74/min, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air. The abdomen is soft, with mild suprapubic fullness. Digital rectal examination finds a smoothly enlarged, non-tender prostate. Urinalysis is negative for protein, blood, nitrite, and leukocytes. Creatinine is 101 µmol/L, and prostate-specific antigen is 3.1 ng/mL. Bedside scanning shows 420 mL post-void residual urine.

Painless red urine appeared twice today after months of weak stream, prolonged hesitancy, and nighttime urination. Abdominal examination is benign, with mild suprapubic fullness. Hemoglobin is 13.9 g/dL, creatinine 109 µmol/L, and leukocyte count 7.6 ×10⁹/L. The abdomen is non-peritonitic, and the prostate feels symmetrically enlarged without nodules. Urinalysis shows trace blood, no leukocytes, and no nitrite. Creatinine is 96 µmol/L.
